alternate_names: Shri Digambar Jain Shantinathji Bara Mandir

history.dynasty: 10th century Jain centre; later superstructure additions
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Digambara Jain temple, keep-or-drop decision needed. The 'Bara Mandir' is the Shantinathji temple at the heart of the Ladnu Jain pilgrimage complex, which comprises five Digambara and two Shvetambara temples; Ladnu became a significant Jain centre in the 10th century with superstructures added in later centuries. The temple is a treasure trove of marble Tirthankara idols, inscribed pillars and old manuscripts; the Shantinath idol sits on an elevated marble vedi with an intricately carved torana. Dated artefacts: 1079 CE torana, 1162 CE Sarasvati idol, 1295 CE inscription on the mulnayak pedestal, bronze idols from 1518-1872. Ladnu is also the birthplace of Acharya Tulsi (ninth head of the Shvetambara Terapanth) and home to Jain Vishva Bharati University (est. 1970). CSV town 'Nagaur' corrected to Ladnun; district corrected from Nagaur to Didwana-Kuchaman (post-2023 reorganisation). Media image was the top image-search result for the specific Bara Mandir query; exact depiction unverified (flag).

name: Digambar Jain Bara Temple, Ladnun
town_description: Ladnun (ancient Chanderi Nagari) is a historic Jain pilgrimage town in Didwana-Kuchaman district, Rajasthan, known for its complex of Digambara and Shvetambara temples and as the seat of Jain Vishva Bharati University.

travel.road: On the Jaipur-Nagaur highway corridor; ~80 km from Nagaur city, close to Sujangarh and Salasar

visitor_information.opening_hours: No published opening hours found (verify). Note: hours listed online for the separate 'Sri Digambar Jain Mahavir Mandir' at Rahu Gate, Ladnun, should not be assumed to apply to the Bara Mandir.
